label: copy phase: input e fed back (mid-recall, not near the end)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or the <DEL> step). It fires when the input is the letter e, i.e. the model has just output e and that e is fed back (94% of activation mass has in_tok = e; small leftovers on w, a, c, q). It requires recall_idx >= 3 and is mostly silent on the last two outputs (to_go <= 1), so it peaks around t = 11-13 in long sequences (L = 8-9). Magnitude depends strongly on the token being output now (the original token right after e): out_tok = a gives about 98% precision and the strongest activations (the top examples are all e followed by a); q, c, w, e, y and t are also high; h almost never fires and k and s fire about 40% of the time. The out-token dependence is graded, with no clean subset, so precision of the simple predicate is only about 0.47 (dev F1 0.57, mass recall 0.86). It does not fire on e during the original phase, on e at recall_idx <= 2, or on other input letters except weakly.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: e, w, a, c, q, v; least: s, j, i, x) and the token being output (most: a, q, e, c, w, t; least: 2, r, -, h); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=9 & t=13.
